name: WA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +15 partisan lean
DelBene's massive fundraising advantage ($3.55M raised vs ~$3K)
Prediction markets price her at ~96% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's +15 Democratic lean, DelBene's incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge over a barely funded challenger all point to a comfortable win, and markets agree at roughly 96%. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, this stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or surprise outside spending against DelBene would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzan DelBene seeks another term in a western Washington district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. She enters the general election as a well-established incumbent with more than $3.5 million raised and over $1.1 million on hand, plus modest outside support and no recorded opposition spending. Republican challenger Mary Silva has raised only a few thousand dollars, leaving her with little capacity to communicate with voters.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price DelBene's chances at roughly 96 percent. The combination of partisan lean, incumbency, and financial dominance makes an upset highly unlikely, though the absence of polling adds some uncertainty to the expected margin.
